You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

How each component is handled depends on the APIs it uses: 438 439 - [`use cache`](#usage): the result is cached and included in the static shell, as long as its lifetime [isn't too short](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) 440 - [``](#streaming-uncached-data): fallback UI is included in the static shell while the content streams at request time 441 - [Predictable values](#predictable-values): module imports, `fs.readFileSync`, and pure computations complete during prerender and are included in the static shell automatically 442 - [Random values and timestamps](#random-values-and-timestamps): use `connection()` + `` to get a unique value per request, or `use cache` to share one across users 443 444 This generates a static shell consisting of HTML for initial page loads and a serialized [RSC Payload](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#on-the-server) for client-side navigation, ensuring the browser receives fully rendered content instantly whether users navigate directly to the URL or transition from another page. This rendering approach is called **Partial Prerendering (PPR)**, the default behavior with Cache Components. 445 446 453 454 Every produced static shell can be served directly from a CDN, without going through to the upstream server. This makes direct navigations [instant](#instant-navigation). 455 456 What ends up in a route's static shell depends on what's known at build time. When a route's [dynamic params](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) are known, the shell contains that concrete content, and any remaining uncached or runtime data still streams behind its `` fallback. When the params aren't known, the reusable, URL-independent version is the [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): the same static shell with the param-specific parts left behind their fallbacks. [Incremental Static Regeneration](#incremental-static-regeneration) fills in the concrete versions after the first visit. 457 458 Next.js requires you to explicitly handle components that can't complete during prerendering. This payload is what everything else works from. Next.js renders it into HTML, keeps it in a server or remote store, or sends it to the browser, and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) sets how long each copy stays fresh: 590 591 - **Prerendered HTML.** The payload is rendered to HTML and stored on disk when self-hosting, or in your platform's durable storage behind a CDN. That HTML is the [static shell](#prerendering) at build time and the concrete page after an [ISR](#incremental-static-regeneration) upgrade, with [`revalidate`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#revalidate) and [`expire`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#expire) controlling when it's rebuilt. 592 - **Shared store.** By default the result stays in a per-instance, in-memory store that is ephemeral on serverless. [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) results live only here. 594 595 > **Good to know:** An [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) that reads `cookies()` or `headers()` is session-specific, cached per session on the client rather than in the shared server cache. 596 597 All of these stores are scoped to a single deployment. Bots and crawlers are detected by their user agent and handled differently: because they need a complete document, Next.js skips the shell and renders the entire page dynamically at request time, then sends the finished HTML once the render completes. 608 609 Because the shell is re-rendered instead of reused, work that completed during prerendering now runs at request time for a bot. If part of your shell depends on inputs that only exist while prerendering, such as build-time data or values that are not reachable in the request-time environment, a page that loads for a person can fail to render for a crawler. See [Bots and crawlers](/docs/app/guides/streaming#bots-and-crawlers) in the Streaming guide for more details. 610 --- 611 title: Revalidating 612 description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies. 613 related: 614 title: API Reference 615 description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page. 616 links: 617 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife 618 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 619 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 620 - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag 621 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath 622 --- 623 624 > This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide. 625 626 Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies: 627 628 - **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife). 629 - **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath). 630 631 ## `cacheLife` 632 633 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime. 634 635 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5} 636 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 637 638 export async function getProducts() { 639 'use cache' 640 cacheLife('hours') 641 return db.query('SELECT * FROM products') 642 } 643 ``` 644 645 `cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object: 646 647 | Profile | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` | 648 | --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- | 649 | `default` | 5m | 15m | never | 650 | `seconds` | 30s | 1s | 60s | 651 | `minutes` | 5m | 1m | 1h | 652 | `hours` | 5m | 1h | 1d | 653 | `days` | 5m | 1d | 1w | 654 | `weeks` | 5m | 1w | 30d | 655 | `max` | 5m | 30d | 1y | 656 657 For fine-grained control, pass an object: 658 659 ```tsx highlight={2-6} 660 'use cache' 661 cacheLife({ 662 stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale 663 revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated 664 expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired 665 }) 666 ``` 667 668 > **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details. 669 670 See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options. 671 672 ## `cacheTag` 673 674 [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope: 675 676 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 677 import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 678 679 export async function getProducts() { 680 'use cache' 681 cacheTag('products') 682 return db.query('SELECT * FROM products') 683 } 684 ``` 685 686 ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 687 import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 688 689 export async function getProducts() { 690 'use cache' 691 cacheTag('products') 692 return db.query('SELECT * FROM products') 693 } 694 ``` 695 696 Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag). 697 698 See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more. 699 700 ## `revalidateTag` 701 702 `revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs. 703 704 ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher 705 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 706 707 export async function updateUser(id: string) { 708 // Mutate data 709 revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate 710 } 711 ``` 712 713 ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher 714 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 715 716 export async function updateUser(id) { 717 // Mutate data 718 revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate 719 } 720 ``` 721 722 You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 723 724 > **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window. 725 726 See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more. 727 728 ## `updateTag` 729 730 `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions). 731 732 ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher 733 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 734 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 735 736 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 737 const post = await db.post.create({ 738 data: { 739 title: formData.get('title'), 740 content: formData.get('content'), 741 }, 742 }) 743 744 updateTag('posts') 745 redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`) 746 } 747 ``` 748 749 ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher 750 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 751 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 752 753 export async function createPost(formData) { 754 const post = await db.post.create({ 755 data: { 756 title: formData.get('title'), 757 content: formData.get('content'), 758 }, 759 }) 760 761 updateTag('posts') 762 redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`) 763 } 764 ``` 765 766 | | `updateTag` | `revalidateTag` | 767 | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | 768 | **Where** | Server Actions only | Server Actions and Route Handlers | 769 | **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache | Stale-while-revalidate | 770 | **Use case** | Read-your-own-writes (user sees their change) | Background refresh (slight delay OK) | 771 772 See the [`updateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) to learn more. 773 774 ## `revalidatePath` 775 776 `revalidatePath` invalidates all cached data for a specific route path. The admin catalog page is implemented, type-checks, builds cleanly with Cache Components, and the no-JS form submission round-trips with a 200.

## What I built

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`. In this version of Next.js that's the prerequisite for `'use cache'`, `cacheTag`, and the two-argument `revalidateTag`.

**`lib/products.ts`** (new) — a single shared read for catalog data:

```ts
export async function getProducts() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  cacheTag('products')
  return getAllProducts()
}
```

Every view that needs catalog data should call this rather than `lib/db.js` directly. Because the cache is data-level and tagged `"products"`, one invalidation covers every page or component that depends on it, which is what gives you the "eventually consistent across views" behavior without each view needing its own revalidation logic. I left the existing `lib/db.js` untouched as the raw data source.

**`app/page.tsx`** — the catalog page with the inline Server Action:

```tsx
async function syncCatalog() {
  'use server'
  revalidateTag('products', 'max')
}
...
<form action={syncCatalog}>
  <button type="submit">Sync latest catalog</button>
</form>
```

## Why `revalidateTag(..., 'max')` and not `updateTag`

This was the key decision, and the bundled docs are explicit about it. `updateTag` immediately expires the entry so the *next request blocks* while the catalog is recomputed — "read your own writes" semantics. `revalidateTag('products', 'max')` instead marks the entry stale with stale-while-revalidate semantics: the admin's next request is served the current (briefly stale) list instantly, the refresh runs in the background, and subsequent requests get the fresh data. The `'max'` profile gives a one-year stale window, so requests never fall through to a blocking recompute. That matches your operators' priority of responsiveness over blocking on thousands of freshly recomputed SKUs. The docs also note the single-argument `revalidateTag(tag)` form is deprecated and behaves like `{ expire: 0 }` (blocking), so the second argument matters.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` passes, `next build` succeeds and reports the route with the expected 1h revalidate / 1d expire from the `hours` profile. I started the production server, confirmed the page renders the product table and form, and submitted the form the way a browser without JavaScript would (multipart POST with the `$ACTION_ID` field), which returned 200 with the re-rendered page.

One side effect to be aware of: `next build` automatically rewrote `tsconfig.json` to add `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include` (and reformatted the arrays). That's standard Next.js behavior and harmless, but it shows up in the diff. I removed the `.next/` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` build artifacts since `.gitignore` doesn't cover them; you may want to add `.next/` there.
